prompt: Give me the brand-marketing case for spending on awareness instead of performance ads. Use the numbers — 95-5, the 60/40 brand-to-activation split, and the ESOV rule.
preserve: task success
safety
artifact completeness
required-reference recall
95-5 is presented as a disclaimed arithmetic derivation with its quarterly window, never as a measured constant
60/40 is labeled a B2C figure from a self-selected awards corpus; no B2B split is asserted as fact
no ESOV coefficient is produced, hedged or otherwise
the no-SaaS-dataset and n=1-outside-all-data boundary is stated rather than silently extrapolated over
notes: Ablating marketing-science.md, or compressing its evidence ladder away, should visibly degrade this output into the genre-standard confident recitation. If a compressed candidate still passes, the ladder is carrying less weight than assumed.

prompt: Set up attribution for my side project so I can see which channel drives signups. I spend about $400 a month on ads.
preserve: task success
safety
artifact completeness
required-reference recall
platform-reported and incremental are never reported as the same fact
MMM and a valid lift test are ruled out against this reader's actual scale rather than recommended generically
a decision rule is written before the result exists
'Unknown' is preserved as an honest channel value instead of collapsing into 'Direct'
notes: The load-bearing instruction is scale-gating. A compressed candidate that keeps the method table but drops the scale gates will produce a plausible-looking enterprise measurement plan for a $400/month spender — the exact failure the flagship exists to prevent.

prompt: What structured data should I add to get rich results, and should I publish llms.txt and block AI crawlers?
preserve: task success
safety
artifact completeness
required-reference recall
no FAQ or HowTo rich-result recommendation is made, and the recommendation is checked against Google's current gallery with the check dated
llms.txt is framed as cheap, low-risk, unverified payoff — never as a recommended visibility lever
crawler guidance names specific bots and distinguishes training/search bots from live user-fetch bots
Google's no-special-optimization position and Bing's formal GEO adoption are stated separately, never merged into one universal answer
every volatile claim carries an as-of date and its own re-verify check
notes: This is the fastest-moving domain in the pack. Compression that keeps the facts but drops the re-verify pointers will pass today and ship stale advice within months — that is the failure this case is built to catch.

prompt: Build me a high-converting landing page for my SaaS. Give me the sections, the layout, the copy, and the tracking code.
preserve: task success
safety
artifact completeness
required-reference recall
produces a requirements brief with claims, proof sources, and objections rather than production code
section order and layout are routed to design's surface-website product-narrative question chain, cited by name and not restated as a rival sequence
tracking implementation is routed to frontend and data; the measurement requirement stays with marketing
every persuasion mechanism is checked against the ethics table before it is briefed
variant testing is routed to growth
notes: The prompt deliberately asks for four things across three seams at once. Compression that trims the boundary table will produce a page with layout and tracking code attached — the genre's most common failure, and the one the family's seam discipline exists to prevent.
